evals.prompt: A Docs issue asks: 'People keep asking how to add a second code repository to an existing fab0 project. Document it.' Which Diátaxis kind is this page, which folder does it go in, and what must it not contain?
evals.expected_output: A how-to page in docs/how-to/. It gives the steps for the goal only (edit repos in fab0.yaml with path, github, owner and key; check out the sibling; run fab0-resolve validate) and links to explanation/multi-repo.md and reference/wiring.md instead of explaining design or listing every field.
assertions: Classifies the page as a how-to
Says explanation and full field reference belong on other pages, linked rather than mixed in

evals.prompt: Write the section headings, in order, of the brief for a Docs run whose intent is 'Audit reference/wiring.md against the core schemas', and give one example finding in the required form.
evals.expected_output: The seven sections in order: Intent, Readers, Sources, Findings, Outline, Acceptance, Open questions. A finding numbered F1 that states what the page says and what the source says, with path:line@sha for both, and whether a docs task fixes it or it needs code.
assertions: Lists exactly Intent, Readers, Sources, Findings, Outline, Acceptance, Open questions in that order
The example finding has an F-number
The example finding cites both sides as path:line@sha
The example finding says whether it is a docs fix or needs code

evals.prompt: Review this sentence proposed for docs/explanation/gates-and-handoff.md: 'When the reviewer rejects a task, fab0 will simply re-run the implementer as many times as needed until it is approved, and then automatically merges the PR.' The resolver sets MAX_REWORK = 2 and the orchestrator never merges.
evals.expected_output: A reject with findings: the claim is false on two counts (at most two re-runs, then escalation to a person; fab0 never merges, merging is a person's approval), plus style findings (future tense 'will', filler 'simply', 'PR' instead of 'pull request').
assertions: Flags the unlimited re-run claim as false, citing the limit of two re-runs before escalation
Flags automatic merging as false: fab0 never merges
Notes at least one style or vocabulary issue (future tense, 'simply', or 'PR')
The verdict is reject, not approve

evals.prompt: A page says: '`when` lets a stage be skipped on a condition over an artifact's fields.' The resolver refuses `when` with 'not supported yet'. How should the page say it?
evals.expected_output: Mark it Planned with its roadmap step, for example '**Planned (step B.4):** `when` will skip a stage…', and say what exists today: the resolver refuses `when` as not supported yet.
assertions: Uses the Planned marker with a roadmap step
States that the resolver refuses it today
